module_title: Fundamental Rights - Articles Breakdown and Writs
introduction: At this level, we will deeply examine the specific articles under each right (like the abolition of untouchability, right to life, right to education) and the 5 types of 'Writs' issued by the Supreme Court.

core_concepts.title: Right to Equality (Articles 14-18)
core_concepts.description: Art 14: Equality before law. Art 15: Prohibition of discrimination (religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth). Art 16: Equality of opportunity in public employment. Art 17: Abolition of Untouchability. Art 18: Abolition of Titles.

core_concepts.title: Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22)
core_concepts.description: Art 19 guarantees 6 freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession). Art 20: Protection in respect of conviction for offenses. Art 21: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty. Art 22: Protection against arrest and detention.

core_concepts.title: Right to Education (Article 21A)
core_concepts.description: Added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002). It makes it a duty of the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.

core_concepts.title: Right Against Exploitation (Articles 23-24)
core_concepts.description: Art 23: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labor (begar). Art 24: Prohibition of employment of children (under 14) in factories/hazardous jobs.

core_concepts.title: The 5 Writs (Under Article 32)
core_concepts.description: 1. Habeas Corpus (To have the body of), 2. Mandamus (We command), 3. Prohibition (To forbid), 4. Certiorari (To be certified/informed), 5. Quo-Warranto (By what authority?).

important_entities.name: Freedom of Press
important_entities.significance: Unlike the US Constitution, the Indian Constitution does not explicitly mention 'Freedom of Press'. It is implicitly covered under 'Freedom of Speech and Expression'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are available ONLY to Indian citizens. All other Fundamental Rights (like 14, 20, 21, etc.) are available to both citizens and foreigners.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Supreme Court vs. High Court Writ Jurisdiction
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Supreme Court (Art 32) can issue writs ONLY for Fundamental Rights. However, High Courts (Art 226) can issue writs for Fundamental Rights AND for 'ordinary legal rights'. Therefore, the writ jurisdiction of the High Court is WIDER than that of the Supreme Court.

exam_strategy_tips: Article 17 (Untouchability) and Article 21A (Education) are SSC and State PCS favorites.
Be prepared for 'Match the Following' questions pairing the Latin writ names (like Mandamus) with their English meanings ('We Command').
